newsitem.title: UK: Capita buys two firms for 11.85 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Capita buys two firms for 11.85 mln stg.

text.p: British outsourcing and support service provider Capita Group Plc Plc said on Friday it had agreed to acquire a pension administrator and full control of a business service firm for a combined sum of 11.85 million stg.
Capita said it had agreed to buy out the remaining 50 percent stake in DriveSafe Services, a business services firm in which Capita and JHP Group have equal control.
Capita would pay 7.5 million stg and issue 394,633 ordinary Capita shares.
It said it might pay a further consideration of five million stg depending on DriveSafe's financial performance.
In a second transaction it has agreed to buy Hartshead Solway, one of UK's largest independent pension administrators for 4.35 million stg.
Capital would also repay a 400,000 stg loan sought by Solway from WPF Holdings Ltd, a holding firm controlled by seven regional water firms.
The acquisition of Hartshead will make Capita the largest provider of pensions administrations in the UK with 1.8 million pensions under managment.

Capita said it had reached an agreement with Close Brothers and Credit Lyonnais Laing for the placement of shares in Hartshead and DriveSafe with institutional investors at a price of 610 pence per share.
Capita said the placement is conditional upon completion of the acquisitions which is expected to occur on February 28.
